subject: can you change the mixture in occuRN

messages.author: d2343caab336f06d
messages.subject: can you change the mixture in occuRN
parts:
Hi All,

Simple question; can you change the mixture used in occuRN (i.e. to a negative binomial)? 

I am analyzing my data with pcount() but I would like to take a look at occupancy in addition to abundance if at all possible.  The only problem is that my data has dispersion issues and the occuRN model does not converge using a Poisson.

My counts range from 0-500 and I only have detection heterogeneity at sites in the 1-10 count range. I would like to adjust for our confidence of occupancy rate at those lower count levels if at all possible so alternative work arounds are welcome! 

Cheers

Adia

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] can you change the mixture in occuRN
parts:
hi Adia,
 you cannot use a NB model in the occuRN function.
 I would generally recommend against this approach for data exhibiting such high variability in counts.
regards,
andy

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] can you change the mixture in occuRN
parts:
hi Adia,
  right, using occuRN is probably not a good idea with such extreme heterogeneity.   The bottom line is coming up with a concise model to explain counts of 0 and 500 is really problematic (even with pcount).
 If the counts are EITHER 0 or relatively high then possibly some kind of zero-inflation model may be appropriate.
regards
andy
